title: "Descriptive Statistics"
format: html

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary-prep
#| ref.label: !expr c("setup", "load-data", "outcomes-long")
#| include: false
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-stats
#| include: false

f2 <- \(x) format(round(x, 2), nsmall = 2)
rng <- \(x) paste0(f2(min(x)), "–", f2(max(x)))
irng <- \(x) if (min(x) == max(x)) min(x) else paste0(min(x), "–", max(x))

# Unrounded statistics for the summary text
s_overall <- describe_outcomes(outcomes, digits = 10)
s_vignette <- describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, digits = 10)
s_condition <- describe_outcomes(outcomes, condition, digits = 10)
s_vig_cond <- describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, condition, digits = 10)
s_vig_status <- describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, status, digits = 10)

n_participants <- n_distinct(outcomes$ResponseId)
n_missing <- sum(is.na(outcomes[c("trust_score", "accept_score", "satisfaction")]))

mean_sd <- \(m) {
  row <- filter(s_overall, measure == m)
  glue::glue("M = {f2(row$mean)}, SD = {f2(row$sd)}")
}
lowest_measure <- as.character(s_overall$measure[which.min(s_overall$mean)])
max_vignette_spread <- s_vignette |>
  summarise(spread = max(mean) - min(mean), .by = measure) |>
  pull(spread) |>
  max()

cond_diff <- \(df) {
  df |>
    select(measure, any_of("vignette"), condition, mean) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = mean) |>
    mutate(diff = Asked - `Not asked`)
}
pooled_cond_diff <- cond_diff(s_condition)
vignette_cond_diff <- cond_diff(s_vig_cond)

status_ranks <- s_vig_status |>
  summarise(
    declined_lowest = mean[status == "Declined both"] == min(mean),
    consented_highest = mean[status == "Consented to both"] == max(mean),
    .by = c(measure, vignette)
  )
n_cells <- nrow(status_ranks)
small_cells <- outcomes |>
  count(vignette, status) |>
  filter(status %in% c("Mixed", "Declined both")) |>
  pull(n)

r_vignette <- cor_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, digits = 10)
r_strongest_pair <- r_vignette |>
  summarise(r = mean(pearson), .by = pair) |>
  slice_max(r, n = 1) |>
  pull(pair) |>
  as.character()

r_cond <- cor_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, condition, digits = 10) |>
  select(vignette, pair, condition, pearson, conf_low, conf_high) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(pearson, conf_low, conf_high)) |>
  mutate(
    asked_higher = pearson_Asked > `pearson_Not asked`,
    ci_overlap = conf_low_Asked <= `conf_high_Not asked` &
      `conf_low_Not asked` <= conf_high_Asked
  )

summary_person_means <- outcomes |>
  summarise(
    across(c(trust_score, accept_score, satisfaction), mean),
    .by = ResponseId
  )
r_between <- cor_outcomes(summary_person_means, digits = 10)
r_within <- rmcorr_outcomes(outcomes, digits = 10)

summary_orders <- outcomes |>
  mutate(cond = if_else(condition == "Asked", "A", "B")) |>
  summarise(cond_order = str_flatten(cond[order(vignette)]), .by = ResponseId)
r_order <- outcomes |>
  left_join(summary_orders, by = join_by(ResponseId)) |>
  rmcorr_outcomes(cond_order, digits = 10)
n_order_ci_include_overall <- r_order |>
  left_join(select(r_within, pair, overall = pearson), by = join_by(pair)) |>
  with(sum(conf_low <= overall & overall <= conf_high))
```

Key descriptive findings for the `r n_participants` participants in the
panel, each of whom rated three vignettes (all outcomes on a 1–5 scale;
`r n_missing` missing scores). Numbers are calculated when the document
renders, but the interpretive wording is not, so re-read it if the data change.

- **Overall levels.** All three measures sit near the scale midpoint: trust
  (`r mean_sd("Trust")`), acceptance (`r mean_sd("Acceptance")`) and
  satisfaction (`r mean_sd("Satisfaction")`), with `r str_to_lower(lowest_measure)`
  lowest. Vignette means for any one measure differ by at most `r f2(max_vignette_spread)`.
- **Condition (asked vs. not asked).** Pooled across vignettes, Asked minus
  Not asked differences range from
  `r f2(min(pooled_cond_diff$diff))` to `r f2(max(pooled_cond_diff$diff))`.
  Within individual vignettes they range
  from `r f2(min(vignette_cond_diff$diff))` to
  `r f2(max(vignette_cond_diff$diff))`, and the Asked mean is higher in
  `r sum(vignette_cond_diff$diff > 0)` of `r nrow(vignette_cond_diff)`
  vignette × measure comparisons. This has not been tested formally.
- **Consent status.** Participants who declined both consent requests gave
  the lowest mean rating in `r sum(status_ranks$declined_lowest)` of
  `r n_cells` vignette × measure cells; those who consented to both gave the
  highest in `r sum(status_ranks$consented_highest)` of `r n_cells`. These
  groups are self-selected and the "Declined both" and "Mixed" cells are small
  (`r irng(small_cells)` per vignette), so this describes who chose what rather
  than an effect of consenting.
- **Correlations among outcomes.** Within each vignette, the outcomes
  correlate at r = `r rng(r_vignette$pearson)`, with
  `r str_to_lower(r_strongest_pair)` the most strongly related pair on
  average. Split by condition, the Asked correlation is higher in
  `r sum(r_cond$asked_higher)` of `r nrow(r_cond)` vignette × pair
  comparisons, and the 95% CIs overlap in `r sum(r_cond$ci_overlap)` of the
  `r nrow(r_cond)` comparisons (overlap is not a formal test).
- **Between- vs. within-person.** Between-person correlations (participant
  means across vignettes) are r = `r rng(r_between$pearson)`; within-person
  (repeated-measures) correlations are r = `r rng(r_within$pearson)`. Split by
  condition order (`r irng(r_order$k)` participants per order), within-person
  correlations range from `r f2(min(r_order$pearson))` to
  `r f2(max(r_order$pearson))`, and their 95% CIs include the overall
  within-person value in `r n_order_ci_include_overall` of
  `r nrow(r_order)` cases.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
source(here::here("scripts", "functions.R"))
```

## Load data

The cleaned data comes from `clean_survey.qmd`. Participants who answered none
of the vignette questions are excluded from the panel.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

data <- read_csv(
  here::here("data", "data_clean.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

panel <- data |>
  filter(if_any(matches("^v[1-3]_status1$"), \(x) !is.na(x)))

tibble(
  respondents = nrow(data),
  excluded = nrow(data) - nrow(panel),
  panel = nrow(panel)
)
```

## Demographics

Ordinal variables are given their natural order; nominal variables are ordered
by frequency.

```{r}
#| label: demo-factors

ai_freq_levels <- c("Never", "Less than monthly", "Monthly", "Weekly", "Daily")

demo <- panel |>
  mutate(
    demo_age = factor(
      demo_age,
      levels = c("18-20", "21-24", "25-29", "30-39", "40 or older")
    ),
    demo_gender = fct_infreq(demo_gender),
    demo_role = fct_infreq(demo_role),
    demo_ai_school_work = factor(demo_ai_school_work, levels = ai_freq_levels),
    demo_ai_personal = factor(demo_ai_personal, levels = ai_freq_levels),
    demo_ai_health = factor(demo_ai_health, levels = c("Yes", "No", "Not sure")),
    demo_field_cat = demo_field_cat |>
      fct_infreq() |>
      fct_relevel("Not currently working", "Other", after = Inf)
  )

# Any values that didn't match the expected levels would show up as NA here
demo |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("demo_") & where(is.factor), \(x) sum(is.na(x))))
```

### Summary table

Percentages are out of participants who answered each question; non-responses
are counted separately as "Unknown".

```{r}
#| label: demo-table

library(gtsummary)

demo |>
  select(starts_with("demo_") & where(is.factor)) |>
  tbl_summary(
    label = list(
      demo_age ~ "Age range",
      demo_gender ~ "Gender",
      demo_role ~ "Role",
      demo_field_cat ~ "Field",
      demo_ai_school_work ~ "AI use for school or work",
      demo_ai_personal ~ "AI use for personal purposes",
      demo_ai_health ~ "Ever used AI for own health"
    ),
    statistic = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)",
    missing_text = "Unknown"
  ) |>
  bold_labels()
```

```{r}
plot_counts(demo, demo_age, "Age range")
```

`clean_survey.qmd`.

```{r}

plot_counts(demo, demo_field_cat, "Field of study or work")
```

## Outcome measures

Trust and acceptance are composite scores (item means, 1–5); satisfaction is a
single 1–5 Likert item. The data are reshaped to one row per participant per
vignette.

Each vignette had two consent requests, so `status1` and `status2` are combined
into a single consent status:

- **Not asked**: condition B (informed only).
- **Consented to both**: condition A, said yes to both requests.
- **Mixed**: condition A, said yes to one request and no to the other.
- **Declined both**: condition A, said no to both requests.

```{r}
#| label: outcomes-long

outcomes <- panel |>
  pivot_vignettes_long() |>
  mutate(
    vignette = factor(vignette, labels = paste0("V", 1:3)),
    condition = factor(
      if_else(status1 == "Was not asked for consent", "Not asked", "Asked"),
      levels = c("Asked", "Not asked")
    ),
    status = case_when(
      status1 == "Was not asked for consent" ~ "Not asked",
      status1 == "Consented to MedHelper" & status2 == "Consented to MedHelper" ~
        "Consented to both",
      status1 == "Did not consent to MedHelper" &
        status2 == "Did not consent to MedHelper" ~ "Declined both",
      !is.na(status1) & !is.na(status2) ~ "Mixed"
    ),
    status = factor(
      status,
      levels = c("Not asked", "Consented to both", "Mixed", "Declined both")
    )
  ) |>
  select(ResponseId, vignette, condition, status, status1, status2,
         trust_score, accept_score, satisfaction)

# Check the status recode and the size of each cell
outcomes |>
  count(vignette, status) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = vignette, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

Some status cells are small (particularly "Mixed" and "Declined both"), so
their summaries should be read with caution.

### Whole sample

Pooled across all three vignettes. Each participant contributes up to three
observations, so these are not independent.

```{r}
#| label: desc-overall

describe_outcomes(outcomes)
```

### By vignette

```{r}
#| label: desc-vignette

describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette)
```

### By condition

Condition is the randomised manipulation: **Asked** (condition A, consent
requested before MedHelper acted) vs. **Not asked** (condition B, informed
afterwards). Unlike consent status, it does not depend on participants'
choices. Condition varied across vignettes within participants, so most people
appear in both groups.

```{r}
#| label: desc-condition

describe_outcomes(outcomes, condition)
```

By vignette:

```{r}
#| label: desc-vignette-condition

describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, condition)
```

Compact layout (mean (SD), n), with the Asked − Not asked difference in means:

```{r}
#| label: desc-vignette-condition-wide

condition_by_vignette <- bind_rows(
  describe_outcomes(outcomes, condition) |> mutate(vignette = "All"),
  describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, condition)
) |>
  mutate(vignette = fct_relevel(as.character(vignette), "All", after = Inf))

condition_by_vignette |>
  mutate(value = glue::glue("{format(mean, nsmall = 2)} ({format(sd, nsmall = 2)}), n={n}")) |>
  select(measure, vignette, condition, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = value) |>
  left_join(
    condition_by_vignette |>
      select(measure, vignette, condition, mean) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = mean) |>
      mutate(diff = Asked - `Not asked`, .keep = "unused"),
    by = join_by(measure, vignette)
  ) |>
  arrange(measure, vignette)
```

Each participant's sequence of conditions across the three vignettes:

```{r}
#| label: condition-sequence

outcomes |>
  mutate(cond = if_else(condition == "Asked", "A", "B")) |>
  summarise(sequence = str_flatten(cond[order(vignette)]), .by = ResponseId) |>
  count(sequence)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-condition
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

outcomes |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(trust_score, accept_score, satisfaction),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("trust_score", "accept_score", "satisfaction"),
      labels = c("Trust", "Acceptance", "Satisfaction")
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = condition, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0.05, alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(measure ~ vignette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.9, 5.1), breaks = 1:5) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Score (1–5)")
```

### By consent status

Pooled across vignettes.

```{r}
#| label: desc-status

describe_outcomes(outcomes, status)
```

### By vignette and consent status

```{r}
#| label: desc-vignette-status

describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, status)
```

Means in a compact wide layout (mean (SD), n):

```{r}
#| label: desc-vignette-status-wide

describe_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, status) |>
  mutate(value = glue::glue("{format(mean, nsmall = 2)} ({format(sd, nsmall = 2)}), n={n}")) |>
  select(measure, status, vignette, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = vignette, values_from = value)
```

## Correlations among outcomes

Pearson correlations are shown with 95% CIs (Fisher z); Spearman correlations
are included because satisfaction is a single ordinal item.

### By vignette

Each vignette has one observation per participant, so these are ordinary
between-participant correlations.

```{r}
#| label: cor-vignette

cor_vignette <- cor_outcomes(outcomes, vignette)
cor_vignette

cor_vignette |>
  mutate(value = glue::glue("{format(pearson, nsmall = 2)} / {format(spearman, nsmall = 2)}")) |>
  select(pair, vignette, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = vignette, values_from = value)
```

The wide table shows Pearson / Spearman.

### By vignette and condition

Within each vignette, the Asked and Not asked groups are different
participants, so the two correlations are independent. Cells have about 29
participants, so the CIs are wide and a difference between conditions would
need to be large to be distinguishable.

```{r}
#| label: cor-vignette-condition

cor_condition <- cor_outcomes(outcomes, vignette, condition)
cor_condition
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-cor-condition
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(
  cor_condition,
  aes(x = pearson, y = fct_rev(condition), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)
) +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_grid(vignette ~ pair) +
  labs(x = "Pearson r (95% CI)", y = NULL)
```

### Between- and within-person correlations

Each participant rated all three vignettes, so the pooled association between
two outcomes mixes two things:

- **Between-person**: do participants who are generally more trusting also
  tend to be more accepting/satisfied? Computed from each participant's mean
  across the three vignettes (n = participants).
- **Within-person**: when a participant rates a vignette higher than their own
  average on one measure, do they also rate it higher on the other? Computed as
  a repeated-measures correlation with `rmcorr::rmcorr()` (Bakdash & Marusich,
  2017), with df = N − k − 1 (N observations, k participants).

Within-person variation includes differences between vignettes and conditions,
so the within-person correlation reflects how the measures move together
across those changes.

```{r}
#| label: cor-between-within

person_means <- outcomes |>
  summarise(
    across(c(trust_score, accept_score, satisfaction), mean),
    .by = ResponseId
  )

cor_levels <- bind_rows(
  cor_outcomes(outcomes) |> mutate(level = "Pooled (all observations)"),
  cor_outcomes(person_means) |> mutate(level = "Between-person"),
  rmcorr_outcomes(outcomes, id = "ResponseId") |> mutate(level = "Within-person")
) |>
  mutate(
    level = factor(
      level,
      levels = c("Pooled (all observations)", "Between-person", "Within-person")
    )
  ) |>
  relocate(level)

cor_levels
```

`k` (participants) and `p_value` are only reported for the within-person
correlations; Spearman is only reported for the others.

The pooled row treats the 3 observations per participant as independent, so
its CI is too narrow; it is shown only for comparison.

```{r}
#| label: plot-cor-between-within
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(
  cor_levels,
  aes(x = pearson, y = fct_rev(level), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)
) +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(vars(pair), ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Pearson r (95% CI)", y = NULL)
```

### Within-person correlations by condition order

Participants saw one of six condition orders across V1–V3 (e.g. `ABA` = asked
in V1, not asked in V2, asked in V3). Within an order, every participant gets
the same vignette/condition combinations, so within-person variation reflects
the same sequence of changes for everyone in that group.

Each order has only about 9–11 participants (df ≈ 2k − 1 ≈ 17–21), so these
CIs are wide. Treat differences between orders as descriptive only.

```{r}
#| label: cor-within-order

condition_orders <- outcomes |>
  mutate(cond = if_else(condition == "Asked", "A", "B")) |>
  summarise(cond_order = str_flatten(cond[order(vignette)]), .by = ResponseId)

cor_order <- outcomes |>
  left_join(condition_orders, by = join_by(ResponseId)) |>
  rmcorr_outcomes(cond_order, id = "ResponseId")

cor_order
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-cor-within-order
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(
  cor_order,
  aes(x = pearson, y = fct_rev(cond_order), xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high)
) +
  geom_pointrange() +
  geom_vline(
    data = filter(cor_levels, level == "Within-person"),
    aes(xintercept = pearson),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(pair)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Within-person r (95% CI)",
    y = "Condition order (V1–V3)",
    caption = "Dashed line: within-person r across all participants"
  )
```

### Satisfaction response distribution

Satisfaction is a single ordinal item, so the full response distribution is
shown alongside the mean.

```{r}
#| label: satisfaction-dist

likert_levels <- c(
  "Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"
)

outcomes |>
  mutate(satisfaction = factor(satisfaction, levels = 1:5, labels = likert_levels)) |>
  count(vignette, status, satisfaction, .drop = FALSE) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1), .by = c(vignette, status)) |>
  mutate(value = glue::glue("{n} ({pct}%)")) |>
  select(-n, -pct) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = satisfaction, values_from = value)
```

### Distributions

```{r}
#| label: plot-outcomes
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7

outcomes |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(trust_score, accept_score, satisfaction),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("trust_score", "accept_score", "satisfaction"),
      labels = c("Trust", "Acceptance", "Satisfaction")
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = status, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0.05, alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(measure ~ vignette) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.9, 5.1), breaks = 1:5) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Score (1–5)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```
